item.text:
**Verdict**
Mixed, but leaning negative. I found some real anti-privilege and procedural-easing moves in 2024, but the dominant pattern is insider recycling, structural favoritism toward state/security-linked actors, and continued suppression of scrutiny and public information.

**Evidence For**
- [Egypt approves regulations to abolish many tax and fee exemptions for state-owned enterprises](https://today.lorientlejour.com/article/1366481/egypt-cabinet-approves-ending-state-enterprise-tax-privileges-.html) — Reuters via L’Orient Today, 2024-01-31: a genuine anti-privilege step, but it still exempted military and national-security activity, so it only partially cut favoritism. QIDs: `7B.9`
- [President Sisi swears in new government ministers](https://sis.gov.eg/en/media-center/news/president-sisi-swears-in-new-government-ministers/) — State Information Service, 2024-07-03: the reshuffle brought in technocratic portfolios in economic management, energy, science, and foreign affairs, which is the clearest pro-competence appointment signal I found. QIDs: `7B.9`
- [Egypt pardons prisoners on Police Day and January 25 Revolution](https://hrightsstudies.sis.gov.eg/en/press/local/egypt-pardons-prisoners-on-Police-Day-and-January-25-Revolution/) — Human Rights Studies - Egypt / SIS, 2024-01-25: Sisi pardoned some prisoners, including people convicted for political expression or political activity. This is a limited positive, but it is episodic clemency rather than a durable break from transactional politics. QIDs: `7B.9`
- [President El-Sisi directs the government to act on National Dialogue recommendations](https://www.presidency.eg/fr/%D9%82%D8%B3%D9%85_%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%A3%D8%AE%D8%A8%D8%A7%D8%B1/%D8%A3%D8%AE%D8%A8%D8%A7%D8%B1-%D8%B1%D8%A6%D8%A7%D8%B3%D9%8A%D8%A9/news2182024/) — Presidency of the Republic of Egypt, 2024-08-21: Sisi publicly ordered action on shorter pretrial detention and alternatives to detention, which is a real procedural easing even if it does not prove deeper institutional independence. QIDs: `7B.9`, also `7B.7`

**Evidence Against**
- [Reuters reports Sisi names ex-defence minister and chief of staff as presidential advisers](https://www.yahoo.com/news/egypts-sisi-names-ex-defence-140545714.html) — Reuters via Yahoo, 2024-07-03: instead of a clean break, the outgoing defense elite were recycled into advisory roles, which looks like managed insider retention. QIDs: `7B.9`, also `7B.5`
- [Egypt replaces head of powerful general intelligence agency](https://www.marketscreener.com/news/latest/Egypt-s-Sisi-replaces-head-of-powerful-general-intelligence-agency-48090165/) — Reuters via MarketScreener, 2024-10-16: the intelligence chief was replaced by his deputy and kept close as an adviser, showing continuity in a politically embedded security network rather than depersonalized staffing. QIDs: `7B.9`, also `7B.5`, `7B.7`
- [Egypt: Spate of Free Speech Prosecutions](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/08/29/egypt-spate-free-speech-prosecutions) — Human Rights Watch, 2024-08-29: authorities detained and prosecuted critics, including cases tied to reporting on a corruption investigation involving senior pro-Sisi party members. That is direct evidence of punishing scrutiny and shielding associates. QIDs: `7B.9`, also `7B.6`, `7B.7`
- [Egypt - Freedom on the Net 2024](https://freedomhouse.org/country/egypt/freedom-net/2024) — Freedom House, 2024: the state continued blocking independent and journalistic sites, allowed censorship without judicial approval, and blocked 562 websites/links by June 2024. This strongly supports information control rather than open access. QIDs: `7B.9`, also `7B.7`, `7B.6`
- [Egypt - Freedom in the World 2024](https://freedomhouse.org/country/egypt/freedom-world/2024) — Freedom House, 2024: corruption is pervasive, Sisi controls the Administrative Control Authority, and the body lacks credibility and the ability to monitor military economic activity. That points to weak safeguards against favoritism and self-dealing. QIDs: `7B.9`, also `7B.6`, `7B.7`
- [2024 Investment Climate Statements: Egypt](https://2021-2025.state.gov/reports/2024-investment-climate-statements/egypt/) — U.S. Department of State, 2024: SOEs and military-owned companies still enjoy regulatory relief and, until recently, tax exemptions; private firms complain about inconsistent enforcement; some firms hold exclusive rights over public assets. This is strong structural evidence of connected-actor privilege. QIDs: `7B.9`, also `7B.4`, `7B.6`
- [HRW: New laws entrench military power over civilians](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/03/05/egypt-new-laws-entrench-military-power-over-civilians) — Human Rights Watch, 2024-03-05: new laws expanded military power over civilians and gave the state tools to pressure businesses. That cuts directly against clean separation from military-economic interests. QIDs: `7B.9`, also `7B.4`, `7B.6`
- [Egypt halt crackdown on people voicing concerns over economic crisis](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/05/egypt-halt-crackdown-on-people-voicing-concerns-over-economic-crisis/) — Amnesty International, 2024-05-13: critics of prices, living conditions, and service failures were arrested, and abuse complaints were not properly investigated. That is selective enforcement against dissent rather than neutral administration. QIDs: `7B.9`, also `7B.7`, `7B.6`

**Search Gap**
I found strong evidence of favoritism toward military/security-linked actors and strong evidence of censorship and selective enforcement. I did **not** find a clean 2024 public record of family-based nepotism or procurement kickbacks tied directly to Sisi himself. The available evidence is mostly structural and institutional: insider recycling, privileged state-linked firms, constrained media access, and selective enforcement.
